items.title: Maple Leaf hopes protein craze will help drive comeback for Yves Veggie brand
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA - Maple Leaf Foods is betting the protein-maxxing trend will help drive a comeback for its Yves Veggie Cuisine brand. Adam Grogan, Maple Leafs Food Chief Operating Officer, stands with Yves veggie cuisine packaging at the company’s Mississauga Offices, as they revive the meat alternative brand, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Chris Young MISSISSAUGA - Maple Leaf Foods is betting the protein-maxxing trend will help drive a comeback for its Yves Veggie Cuisine brand. Chief operating officer Adam Grogan says there’s an unrelenting appetite for protein among consumers, partly fuelled by social media, which has more people opting for protein-first diets, whether it’s sourced from animals or plants. Maple Leaf has revived the 40-year-old plant-based meat brand, which was discontinued last year as demand for meat substitutes declined. Grogan agrees that consumer demand for plant-based meats isn’t what it used to be about a decade ago, when investors poured money into brands such as Beyond Meat. Still, the company sees growth among Yves’ core consumers — vegans, vegetarians and flexitarians. -based plant-protein production facilities earlier this week.

items.title: Vote From Front Door program expands access to the 2026 Municipal Election
items.summary: Homebound residents who are unable to vote in person or appoint a proxy may qualify for a home visit from trained election officials. For some residents, getting to a voting location isn’t possible. That’s why the City of Mississauga is introducing the Vote From Front Door program for the 2026 Municipal Election. The program gives eligible residents who cannot travel to a voting location and cannot appoint a proxy another way to cast their ballot, helping more people participate in local democracy. Through scheduled home visits, trained election officials will help eligible residents through the voting process. As a pilot program, availability is limited to 40 appointments. The Elections Office will review each request and make the final decision on eligibility. If you are interested in participating, you can complete the online Vote From Front Door registration form. Approved applicants will receive appointment details and instructions from the Elections Office before their scheduled voting appointment. ca to learn more about voter eligibility and complete the registration form. With only 40 appointments available, eligible residents are encouraged to apply.

items.title: Your first municipal vote: What to expect on Election Day, October 26
items.summary: Voting for the first time can feel like a big step. Learn what to expect from the moment you arrive at your voting location to the moment you cast your ballot. Voting for the first time is an exciting milestone for many people. It’s also an opportunity to help shape decisions that affect daily life in Mississauga. Whether you’ve recently become eligible to vote or are participating in a municipal election for the first time, you may have questions about what to expect. The good news? You’re not alone. In fact, casting your ballot is easier than you might think. Your first voting experience starts before you arrive at a voting location. Take some time to learn about the candidates running in your ward and the issues that matter most to you. Maybe you’re interested in transit, parks and recreation, housing or how Mississauga will grow in the years ahead. Whatever your priorities, Election Day is your chance to have your say. Before heading out, make sure you know where to vote and have acceptable identification with you. If you received a voter notification card, bring it along.
